items.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020
items.q: Charlie Parker was really good. He did a great job of documenting the world that he inhabited.

ctx.x: Well this has been a fascinating conversation. Thanks, Michelle for setting it up and again, the video you provided us with is really wonderful. I can’t wait to see the complete program and that someday down the road we’ll see you in person.

And I want to add one thing about the video process, much like the process of creating music. You never want to try to recreate something. That’s sort of a losing battle. Charlie Parker was really good. He did a great job of documenting the world that he inhabited. So when I tried to figure out well what’s the next step given this pandemic I said well let’s not try to recreate a live experience. But what we want to do is take a look at the format that we’re utilizing and look at the assets of that format and…

find it to be really different — I find it to be really insightful. I learned more about what’s happening in the music as a viewer in the video platform than I do live. When it’s live I feel more the whole thing. But in this someone doing something interesting, and an attack over there and things that I wouldn’t always catch.
